application_guidance.input_pattern: Full-information exp-concave tracking with unknown comparator movement.
read_original_when: Changing feedback, parameter normalization, horizon regime or the blocked construction.
sensitive_conditions: The all-path upper square-root branch is sqrt(T(1+P)), not sqrt(TP).
The lower bound is worst-sequence expected regret, not probability-2/3 success.
The lower ball example does not prove the same lower bound for every compact domain.
Static signs alone do not establish the dynamic branches.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Upper every realized sequence; lower worst deterministic sequence/comparator expected regret
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Upper O constants depend only on fixed D,G,eta; lower c,c0 are universal
complexity_scope.oracle: Upper revealed-loss full information and multiple base-point evaluations; lower revelation of the entire current coordinate-square function after prediction
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Proper online predictions; cumulative dynamic regret with Euclidean comparator path budget
complexity_scope.regime: All paths for upper; lower and normalized matching require T>=c0 d^2
complexity_scope.resource: Upper adds O(log(2T)) loss/gradient evaluations and Euclidean projections per round; curved internal work O((d^3+C_proj(d))log^2(2T)); lower horizon T, no oracle-query cap claim
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper: outer mixture of SparseGauss and a logarithmic projected-gradient grid. Lower: every causal randomized learner, without a computational restriction.

content.intended_use: Record the complete all-path upper and normalized minimax lower statements without changing feedback or expectation conventions.

dependencies: Imported source interface: Lemma B.13, p.21
map: Run PGD experts z_{t+1}=Pi_W(z_t-alpha grad f_t(z_t)) on alpha_j=2^j D/(G sqrt(T)), j=0,...,ceil(log_2 sqrt(2T)), alongside the curved learner. Each base runs at its own prediction.
Lemma B.13 supplies (D^2+2D P_T)/(2alpha)+alpha G^2 T/2. A grid step within factor two of the optimum gives O(G sqrt(T(D^2+D P_T))).

An outer exponential-weights master at rate eta on original losses predicts the feasible weighted mean and pays at most eta^(-1)log O(log(2T)) meta-regret. This requires separate evaluations of the original losses and gradients at base points.

B.17 uses the clipped curved guarantee within its window. Outside that window the PGD branch is bounded by the static-plus-curved expression, justifying the displayed unconstrained curved term inside the minimum. Lipschitzness supplies GDT cap. Absorb outer overhead and fixed regularity parameters to obtain Corollary 4.2.

dependencies: Imported source interfaces: Lemmas C.2–C.3 and Theorem C.4, pp.27–29
map: Regularity: grad f=(w_j-y)e_j, Hessian=e_j e_j^T, |w_j-y|<=3/2; hence gradient bound 3/2 and Hessian >=(4/9)grad f grad f^T on the radius-1/2 ball.

C.2: for 1<=m<=d and C m/sqrt(T)<=P<=c T/m^2, choose K=ceil(C1(TP^2/m^2)^(1/3)), n=floor(T/(Km)), a=P/(4K), theta=a/sqrt(m). Constants ensure 2<=K<=T/(2m), a<=1/2. In each block draw m independent signs; comparator u^(k)=a(S_k,1,...,S_k,m,0,...,0)/sqrt(m). Cycle m coordinates n times, revealing fresh labels of means theta S_k,j. Total movement <=2a(K-1)<=P.

Equation (58) gives conditional expected excess (w_j-theta S_k,j)^2/2. Since n theta^2<=TP^2/(16K^3m^2)<=1/32, C.1 gives E Reg>=c T theta^2>=c m^(1/3)T^(1/3)P^(2/3). Leftover rounds keep the last conditional mean and have nonnegative expected excess.
C.3 supplies static Omega(d) at zero path length using fixed signs and d observations per coordinate. This is separate from the moving block family.

C.4: use static bound when P<C_*d/sqrt(T), m=d for C_*d/sqrt(T)<=P<=c_*T/d^2, and m=floor(kappa sqrt(T/P)) for c_*T/d^2<P<=bT, where kappa=sqrt(c_*)/2 and b=kappa^2/4. Enlarge c0 so C_*d/sqrt(T)<=min{c_*T/d^2,bT} and c_*T/d^2>=(C_*kappa)^(2/3). These choices validate the block range and produce the curved then square-root branches. At P=bT obtain Omega(T); monotonicity extends saturation to larger P.

The static and dynamic lower bounds concern the same class; max{a,b}>=(a+b)/2 supplies additive d. Conditioning on learner randomness and averaging over generated instances gives a deterministic admissible pair with the same expected-over-learner lower bound.

assumptions: Upper: each differentiable convex f_t is eta-exp-concave on W and has ||grad f_t(w)||_2<=G everywhere. D,G,eta>0 are fixed independently of d,T.

Upper: full information after each prediction permits evaluation of the revealed loss and gradient at every base prediction. Exact Mahalanobis projection is available for arbitrary positive-definite metrics at cost C_proj(d). Dense spectral arithmetic is charged separately.

Lower: causal learners predict in W_d before observing each coordinate-square loss. They may be randomized and computationally unrestricted. No projection assumption restricts the lower-bound learner.
statement.conclusion: Upper: Reg_T(u)<=O_{D,G,eta}(d Lambda_T^2+min{d^(1/3)Lambda_T^(4/3)T^(1/3)P_T(u)^(2/3),sqrt(T(1+P_T(u))),T}). It requires O(log(2T)) loss evaluations, gradient evaluations and Euclidean projections per round in addition to the curved branch's internal work. Lower: inf_A sup E_A Reg_T>=c[d+min{d^(1/3)T^(1/3)P^(2/3),sqrt(TP),T}]. Consequently the worst-domain normalized proper full-information minimax frontier is d+min{d^(1/3)T^(1/3)P^(2/3),sqrt(TP),T} up to polylogarithmic factors for T>=c0 d^2. Upper near-linearity is in T with explicit dimension and projection costs.
statement.objects_and_definitions: d,T are positive integers. Reg_T(u)=sum_t[f_t(w_t)-f_t(u_t)], P_T(u)=sum_{t=2}^T||u_t-u_{t-1}||_2, Lambda_T=1+log(2T). Upper domain W is nonempty compact convex in R^d of Euclidean diameter at most D. Lower domain W_d={w:||w||_2<=1/2}, with losses f_{j,y}(w)=(w_j-y)^2/2 for j in [d], y in {-1,+1}.
statement.parameter_domains: Upper: every comparator path, all T>=1. Lower: T>=c0 d^2, every nonnegative path budget P. Lower normalization D=1, G<=3/2, eta>=4/9 holds uniformly in d.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: Upper: there exists a proper learner independent of comparator and P_T such that for every realized admissible loss sequence and every comparator path the upper bound holds. Lower: there exist universal c,c0>0 such that for every d,T with T>=c0 d^2 and every P>=0, inf_A sup_{deterministic f_1:T of the specified form, u in W_d^T with P_T(u)<=P} E_A Reg_T(u) is bounded below as stated. The worst pair may depend on A; expectation is over learner randomness.
